name: Kristin Hersh
label: 4AD
lede: She never meant to have a solo career: a tape of leftover acoustic songs got to Michael Stipe, he phoned, and three decades later she's still making records in a Rhode Island studio, alongside Throwing Muses, a loud trio and a shelf of books.

hero.by: Kristin Hersh Electric Trio at ONCE, Somerville, June 20, 2019. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A double concussion in Newport
eras.text: Hersh grew up in Newport, Rhode Island, started Throwing Muses with her stepsister Tanya Donelly as a teenager, and made them the first American band on 4AD. The solo career came out of a contract, not a plan.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · The Guardian: Kristin Hersh reader interview
years.h: Born in Atlanta, raised Buddhist by hippie parents
years.p: The family moves to Newport when she's six. Her father gives her a guitar at nine; at eleven her mother marries the father of her best friend, Tanya Donelly.

years.src: NPR: Kristin Hersh on Surviving 18 · The Guardian: Kristin Hersh reader interview
years.h: A car hits her bicycle, and sounds start turning into songs
years.p: Hersh, 16, suffers a double concussion. Afterward, she has said, ambient noise came to her as syllables and drums.
years.xp: "I had a double concussion, and it seemed to trigger this interpretation of ambient noise as music," she told NPR in 2010. Asked in 2026 whether the Muses would have sounded different without the accident, she said yes: people might have liked them more, "but we would have been more forgettable."

q: I was always convinced I wasn't a manic depressive, I was a songwriter
years.src: NPR: Kristin Hersh on Surviving 18 · Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · The Guardian: Kristin Hersh reader interview
years.h: Diagnosed bipolar at 18, and pregnant the same year
years.p: The year Throwing Muses lands a 4AD deal is the year her first son is on the way. It becomes the subject of her memoir Rat Girl.
years.xp: Of the pregnancy, she told NPR: "That baby probably saved my life, far more than the medication could have." She later spoke publicly about further diagnoses and about treating post-traumatic and dissociative disorders with EMDR, which she told the Guardian is "like psychological chemo."

eras.title: The tape Michael Stipe picked up
eras.text: To get Throwing Muses off Warner Bros. without breaking up the band, Hersh owed another record. She had a tape of acoustic leftovers, a cellist and a producer who'd played guitar for Patti Smith. It became the highest-charting album of her career.

years.big: "He called me up and said: 'I love this tape.'"
q: I wasn't ever going to have a solo career
years.src: The Guardian: Kristin Hersh reader interview · Wikipedia: Your Ghost
years.h: [[Michael Stipe|905a8f9b-03dc-4f47-b9bb-ecce7ea13ab1]] phones the studio and ends up on Your Ghost
years.p: Hersh was struggling with the vocal when Stipe of [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] called. She realized the song needed his voice. It goes to No. 1 in Iceland and No. 45 in the UK.
years.xp:
"I had to get off Warner Brothers and breaking up the band wasn't going to work," Hersh told Guardian readers in 2026. Stipe, she says, knew she'd mess up the recording because she didn't care.

The song is about getting past the death of a close friend. Katherine Dieckmann's video is a homage to Maya Deren's 1943 film Meshes of the Afternoon. Years later Stipe turned up unannounced at a solo show in New York and sang his part from the back of the room.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hips and Makers
years.h: Hips and Makers goes Top 10 in Britain
years.p: Voice, acoustic guitar and Jane Scarpantoni's cello, produced with [[Lenny Kaye|47455aa4-c71e-4662-a775-33b81fcf0a37]] at Stable Sound in Portsmouth, Rhode Island. It reaches No. 7 in the UK and No. 1 on the indie chart.
years.xp: 4AD released it in the UK on January 24, Sire in the US a week later. Hersh described it as "full of skin and coffee, shoes and sweat and babies and sex and food and stores." No Throwing Muses album or later solo record has charted higher in Britain. The finished Muses album, University, waited until it was out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh
years.h: She and her husband start their own label, ThrowingMusic
years.p: Hersh and her husband and manager, Billy O'Connell, set it up to control her recordings. A download-subscription service, Works in Progress, follows.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Wikipedia: Throwing Muses
years.h: Throwing Muses stop, and solo becomes the main job
years.p: After Limbo on Rykodisc the band goes quiet. Bassist [[Bernard Georges|485f3e4b-9712-4988-83b0-e6afe2916ecd]] keeps playing with Hersh.

eras.title: Stable Sound, mostly alone
eras.text: Through the late '90s Hersh made records at Steve Rizzo's Stable Sound in Portsmouth, Rhode Island, playing more and more of the instruments herself. 4AD kept releasing them in Europe while American labels came and went.

years.cap: Ticket for Hersh at Henry Wood Hall, Glasgow, March 22, 1998
years.src: Wikipedia: Strange Angels
years.h: Strange Angels is dedicated to a band that just stopped
years.p: Co-produced with Joe Henry and Steve Rizzo, out on 4AD in Europe and Rykodisc elsewhere. The sleeve reads "for Billy, Dylan, Ryder, Wyatt and TM (1984–1997)."
years.xp: Reviews split. Entertainment Weekly's Will Hermes called it some of her strongest music ever; the Guardian's Caroline Sullivan said it was "either heaven or hell" depending on your tolerance for Hersh's voice. It reached No. 7 on the UK indie chart.

years.src: Wikimedia Commons: Kristin Hersh
years.h: Solo at Roskilde
years.p: Hersh plays the Danish festival the summer Strange Angels comes out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Wikipedia: Belly (band)
years.h: Sky Motel, and Tom Gorman of Belly on the tour
years.p: Hersh keeps a record-a-year pace and posts solo releases online. [[Belly|c118bc97-11a7-41dc-a55e-48c3bcf22ac2]]'s guitarist Tom Gorman joins her on the road.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sunny Border Blue · Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh
years.h: She plays nearly everything on Sunny Border Blue
years.p: Recorded at Stable Sound through 2000 and produced by Hersh. The one cover is Cat Stevens's Trouble; Metacritic averages 81.
years.xp: Hersh has described songwriting in this period as a way to turn ugly feelings into art. Around these records she worked with [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]], Willard Grant Conspiracy, Grant-Lee Phillips and John Doe.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Wikipedia: Throwing Muses
years.h: The Grotto and a Throwing Muses album, same day
years.p: Acoustic sketches set in Providence, with Andrew Bird on violin and [[Howe Gelb|9896989a-cfdb-4ec9-8bd5-4dbd33982cef]] on piano. The Muses' second self-titled album comes out alongside it.

eras.title: Louder, and free to download
eras.text: With David Narcizo unable to tour full time, Hersh built a power trio and started giving music away. Fans could subscribe to her the way you'd back a theater company, and she wrote down the year that started it all.

years.cap: 50 Foot Wave at Easy Street Records, February 2004
years.src: Wikipedia: 50 Foot Wave · Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Louisville Public Media: Kristin Hersh
years.h: [[50 Foot Wave|b2d1207f-bc0e-4228-9d29-874973960f04]] is named for the lowest F you can hear
years.p: Hersh, Georges and drummer Rob Ahlers go loud and fast. The name is the length of the sound wave of the lowest audible F.
years.xp: The trio's first records came out through ThrowingMusic and 4AD in 2004 and 2005, and much of what followed went out under Creative Commons licenses, with fans invited to share and remix it. Hersh assigns guitars by project: a Tele or Strat for the Muses, a Les Paul Junior for 50 Foot Wave, a Collings for solo songs.

years.cap: Hersh at Music Millennium, Portland, February 2007
years.src: Wikipedia: Learn to Sing Like a Star
years.h: Learn to Sing Like a Star, her first solo album in four years
years.p: Yep Roc has it in the US, 4AD everywhere else. Narcizo plays drums, Martin and Kimberlee McCarrick play cello and violin, and Trina Shoemaker mixes in Nashville.
play: Learn to Sing Like a Star

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Irish Times: Kristin Hersh
years.h: CASH Music: $30 a quarter, or $5,000 for a producer credit
years.p: Hersh and [[Donita Sparks|03b6f1e2-70b5-46c9-b290-193d31289fee]] of [[L7|57111f1f-9829-45ea-bb4e-a5aba37cd1d1]] launch a direct-to-fan site. Subscribers, called Strange Angels, get albums, downloads and guest-list spots.
years.xp: The top tier bought an executive producer credit on her next album. "You can't play music to make money. You just can't," she told the Irish Times in 2023. Her 2008 album Speedbath went out under a Creative Commons license.

years.cap: Hersh and Tanya Donelly, Brattle Theatre, Cambridge, October 6, 2007
years.src: Wikimedia Commons: Kristin Hersh
years.h: Hersh and Donelly share the Brattle stage in Cambridge
years.p: The stepsisters who started Throwing Muses play together at the Brattle Theatre in Harvard Square.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · NPR: Kristin Hersh on Surviving 18
yt: Rock Book Show interview on Rat Girl
years.h: Rat Girl turns a teenage diary into a memoir
years.p: Built from the diary she kept at 18, the year of the 4AD deal, her diagnosis and her first pregnancy. In Britain it's Paradoxical Undressing.
years.xp: The book also covers her friendship with the actress Betty Hutton, who was a student at Salve Regina University in her sixties and came to early Muses shows. Rob Sheffield called it an "uncommonly touching punk memoir" in the New York Times; Rolling Stone later ranked it No. 8 among the greatest rock memoirs. The same year Hersh put out Crooked as a download and a hardback with an essay for every track.

eras.title: Books, sons and Fire Records
eras.text: After her marriage ended, Hersh wrote more books than ever, found a home on Fire Records and kept a solo album, a Muses album or a 50 Foot Wave record coming every year or two, several of them named for real roads.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh
years.h: Hersh and Billy O'Connell divorce after 25 years
years.p: O'Connell had managed her and co-run ThrowingMusic. They have four sons.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh · Irish Times: Kristin Hersh
years.h: Don't Suck, Don't Die: a book about Vic Chesnutt
years.p: Hersh writes about her friendship with [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]], who died in 2009, and what she learned from his songs.
years.xp: She credited Chesnutt with teaching her about "fluid timing and the grace of a melody that breaks the rules of meter." A book of lyrics, Nerve Endings, followed in 2018, and Seeing Sideways: A Memoir of Music and Motherhood in 2021, about raising four boys on a tour bus.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wyatt at the Coyote Palace
years.h: Twenty-four songs, sold as a book
years.p: A double album packaged with a book through Omnibus Press. Metacritic averages 80; Drowned in Sound gives it 9 out of 10.

years.src: Wikipedia: Possible Dust Clouds · Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh
years.h: Possible Dust Clouds, her first for Fire Records
years.p: Signed in June, out in October: ten songs in 36 minutes, cut in Rhode Island and San Francisco with Steve Rizzo.

years.cap: Hersh, Rob Ahlers and Fred Abong, ONCE, Somerville, June 2019
years.src: Wikimedia Commons: Kristin Hersh · Wikipedia: Kristin Hersh
yt: Electric Trio at Terminal West, Atlanta, June 2019
years.h: The Electric Trio puts Fred Abong back beside her
years.p: Hersh tours as the Kristin Hersh Electric Trio, with Ahlers on drums and [[Fred Abong|d756e807-10da-4fee-9a32-7d76ce120b4b]], the former Throwing Muses and Belly bassist. By 2020 Hersh and Abong are engaged.

years.src: Louisville Public Media: Kristin Hersh · Irish Times: Kristin Hersh
years.h: She trashes a whole album, then makes Clear Pond Road
years.p: "It was fine. It just wasn't this one," she says of the scrapped record. The title came off a street sign she found in a junk shop.
years.xp: The sign became a talisman for Hersh and her youngest son, Bodhi, now a professional surfer. The songs move between New Orleans and Southern California, with strings and mellotron around the guitar.

years.src: The Guardian: Kristin Hersh reader interview
years.h: Back in Providence, on a street called Hope
years.p: Sugar on Blackstone, on Fire, is autobiographical: stories from childhood, some from the 1970s. Dark Eyed Junco is about her and her little brother.
years.xp: Hersh was living on Hope Street, off Blackstone Boulevard, while making it. "So I had 'Hope' on the one side and the ship of lost souls on the other," she told Guardian readers. Dark Eyed Junco remembers the two kids shooting baskets until dark rather than going home to their stepfather.
